# lean-pkg doctor

installation, registry, index and tool diagnostics; exit 1 when the registry is unreadable or its schema version is unsupported.

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg doctor [--fetch] [--upgrade-from OLD] [--to NEW] [--source DIR] [common flags]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `--fetch` | git fetch origin in the tool checkout and the registry repo before comparing (default: local refs) |
| `--upgrade-from OLD` | instead of the diagnostics: what changed for a package author since OLD (a version, 0.9.0 / v0.9.0, or any commit of the lean-pkg repository): formats, on-disk keys, commands, flags, --json keys, aliases, Python floor, packaged files, and the curated behaviour changes of docs/upgrades/; read-only (docs/design/upgrade-preflight.md) |
| `--to NEW` | with --upgrade-from: the newer version or commit (default HEAD of the source) |
| `--source DIR` | with --upgrade-from: the lean-pkg git checkout to read both trees from (default: the checkout this lean-pkg runs from) |

## Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `doctor` | one `ok`/`warn`/`n/a` line each: version; install kind and path (an editable install inside a git checkout adds its short HEAD, branch, and behind/ahead counts against `origin/<branch>`, from local refs unless `--fetch`); registry path and schema version, ending `[source: flag|env|user-default|cwd]` (`doctor --json` adds `"source"` to that check); `user-default`: what `~/.lean-pkg/registry` points at (`ok`) or `n/a` when it is not set up; events path, ending `[source: flag|registry-sibling|env|sibling]`; `registry-repo`: the git work tree holding the registry with its HEAD, branch, behind/ahead of `origin/<branch>` (or "no origin remote" when there is none) and uncommitted tracked files, naming the registry files among them (`warn` when behind, ahead, detached, or the registry files are uncommitted: do not write from there yet; `n/a` outside a work tree); `leases`: live count, leases lapsing within 2 h and expired-but-unswept ones by name, and leases whose fields cannot be parsed (`warn` when any is non-empty); `time`: naive (offset-less, legacy) lease `claimed_at` / history `ts` values, read as UTC (`warn` when any); index path and entry count, ending `[source: flag|env|registry-sibling|cwd]`; `host`: the `comparator host-check` verdict (`warn` when this host cannot produce comparator receipts); `lake`, `lean`, `elan`, `git`, `gh`, `reuse`, `bwrap`, `comparator`, `nanoda`, `go`, `cargo`, `jq` on PATH (an `n/a` tool line says what the tool is for and when it is needed, so a host that only reads the registry still has a clean doctor: `comparator`, `nanoda`, `bwrap`, `go`, `cargo` and `jq` only produce comparator receipts on this host, `go`, `cargo` and `jq` being what `lean-pkg receipt comparator` needs to build the legacy comparator tools; `reuse` is the release gate's REUSE lint only; `gh` serves `promote`, `audit` and `reservoir check`; a `lake` or `lean` that is not elan's proxy in `$ELAN_HOME/bin`, default `~/.elan/bin`, is a `warn`, since it ignores each project's `lean-toolchain`; without `bwrap`, the `tool comparator` line adds "run `lean-pkg comparator host-check` to see whether this host can produce receipts", see [which hosts can produce receipts](../comparator.md#which-hosts-can-produce-receipts)); `gh auth`: the github.com account from `gh auth status` (`warn` when gh is present but not logged in, since `promote` and `audit` need it; `n/a` without gh); Python version. A check that raises prints `warn <item>: internal error ...` and the others still run. Exit 1 when the registry is unreadable or its schema version is unsupported (a missing registry counts as unreadable), else 0 | `[--fetch]` |
| `doctor --upgrade-from OLD` | instead of the checks above, the **upgrade preflight**: what changed for a package author between two lean-pkg versions or commits (even when the version string is unchanged), read from a lean-pkg git checkout's objects and never by running the old code. Mechanical: `requires-python`, dependencies, executables, format markers (every `x/N` constant, the registry version, the formalization.yaml version), the on-disk key lists (registry package and lease, lower-tier and comparator receipts, formalization.yaml's derived keys), command paths and options from the help goldens (a renamed command or flag whose old spelling is an alias is `renamed`, not removed), the `--json` key sets, the alias tables and the packaged data files. Curated: the entries of `docs/upgrades/<version>.yaml` whose pull request lies in OLD..NEW (`behavior[]`, `breaking[]`), and the range's pull requests no record names (`uncurated[]`). OLD and NEW are a version (`0.10.0`: tag `v0.10.0`, else the `release: 0.10.0` commit) or any revision; `--json` schema `lean-pkg-upgrade/1`; read-only, no registry, no network; see [the design](../design/upgrade-preflight.md) and [the 0.11.0 notes](../upgrades/0.11.0.md) | `--upgrade-from OLD` `[--to NEW]` `[--source DIR]` |

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

Exit 1 is also a negative answer here:

- `doctor`: the registry is unreadable or its schema version is unsupported

## Examples

Check the installation, the registry, the index and the tools in one line each; exit 1 when the registry is unreadable or its schema version is unsupported.

```bash
lean-pkg doctor
```
